page: Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across multi-core operations and memory bandwidth. The instance achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 13988.78 and a PassMark memory score of 2186.5. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 753.02 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 87.05 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register in the lower performance bracket.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5b.4xlarge provides a high-density memory configuration relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of higher-tier compute instances. It performs in the middle tier for database operations, processing 13.15 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 5119.53 on PassMark database operations. This profile is appropriate for relational databases, in-memory caching, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM but moderate CPU throughput.
